newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EVN seeks cooperation with local gas firm.
newsitem.headline: EVN seeks cooperation with local gas firm.

text.p: Lower Austrian utility Energieversorgung Niedersoesterreich (EVN) said on Thursday it no longer wanted to buy a stake in regional gas supplier BEGAS but instead was seeking a cooperation deal.

BEGAS has been looking for an outside partner to help it meet an expected rise in gas demand in the south-eastern province of Burgenland. A new Lenzing fibre plant, due to open there this autumn, will be a major future customer.
"Today EVN submitted an attractive cooperation proposal to the majority shareholders, the gas-consuming communities of Burgenland," EVN said in a statement.
BEGAS-Gemeindeanteilsverwaltungs AG (GAV), a holding company representing 73 Burgenland communities, has a 51.86 percent stake in BEGAS.
EVN had originally been chasing a 25 percent direct stake in BEGAS but had come up against stiff competition from Austria's biggest industrial group, oil and gas firm OMV.
OMV, by far the nation's biggest gas carrier, has said it will bid for a 49 percent stake in GAV but settle for 39 percent with 10 percent going to BEGAS.
"This seems to be the preferred option in Burgenland," OMV Chief Executive Richard Schenz said earlier this week.
EVN insisted on Thursday it was offering the better deal.
"In EVN's opinion a tie-up with a (gas) carrier could impinge on free competition and would limit BEGAS's independence to the detriment of its customers," it said.
EVN said a cooperation with it would bring advantages in transport, storage and distribution and help to expand gas supplies in Burgenland.
"It would also guarantee that BEGAS remained in Burgenland hands," it added. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 254
